findings.reason: the anchor is the only statement of the WEST row's inputs, so naming the landed revision or carrying the recipe inline keeps the endpoint reachable after the peer tree goes.
findings.text: the §9 input anchor resolves today but is fragile: `git cat-file -e 403337a04:scripts/west_forward_iron/machine.py` succeeds and its content matches §9's stated inputs (EQUILIBRIUM_DD 3.42.2, SLICE 14, CELL_SIZE 0.08, PULSE_DD 4.1.0), yet the path does not exist at HEAD and the commit is no ref's ancestor (`git for-each-ref --contains 403337a04` prints nothing; its only reachability is the detached HEAD of worktree .../icm-forward-solve-iron, which reckon removes after promotion)

findings.reason: §9's done-when requires every centroid-constrained row to reach the joint acceptance, and a predicate that holds the 110/300/1000-cell rows to 1e-2 relative sup refuses all of them, sending the section node to a gate it cannot pass by building the predicate correctly.
findings.text: §7's predicate clause reads "map fidelity where an analytic state exists", while §6 (:79) binds map fidelity "on the analytic certificate rows" and §4 (:63) states the centroid-constrained rows "are not held to this bound, which their coarse rungs cannot meet"; the centroid-constrained certificate is an analytic state, so the predicate as written applies a clause §6 deliberately excludes

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §9 pins its WEST input recipe to scripts/west_forward_iron/machine.py at 403337a04, which is the detached HEAD of a live peer plan's unlanded worktree (icm-forward-solve-iron) and is absent from the branch tree, so it stops resolving once that tree is removed.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's done-when drops the receipt-reproduction clause that the followup it carries (f-cfs-legacy-read-migration) makes part of the same done.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no section routes a record to a scratch or node-local path, and §9 requires the per-row records and poloidal panels that the evidence surface carries.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed sections carry no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into a name or comment; dates and lead rulings appear only as dated provenance.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7 scopes its map-fidelity clause to "where an analytic state exists", which takes in the centroid-constrained certificate rows that §4 and §6 exclude from that clause because their coarse rungs cannot meet the bound, so the predicate §9 is judged against would refuse rows §9 requires to reach the joint acceptance.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each node names one deliverable; §6's acceptance table is the specification its retirement clause is judged by rather than a second build, and §9's three clauses are one route's rows.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 declares no depends-on (plan-section-depends-on names no s5) and no section lists §2, §3 or §4 as a predecessor, yet §5's first done-when clause is a terminal residual on the analytic certificate the map of §4 must serve.
